knowledge_graph.title: President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief
knowledge_graph.description: The United States President's Emergency Plan For AIDS Relief is the global health funding by the United States to address the global HIV/AIDS epidemic and help save the lives of those suffering from the disease. As of 2023, PEPFAR has saved over 25 million lives, primarily in sub-Saharan Africa.

related_questions.question: How long can you live with AIDS without knowing?

text_blocks.snippet: A person can live with HIV for many years, possibly a decade or more, without knowing they are infected. Without treatment, HIV progresses to AIDS, but this can take a significant amount of time, and many people with HIV experience no noticeable symptoms for years, especially in the early stages.
snippet_highlighted_words: many years, possibly a decade or more

list.title: Early Stages:
list.snippet: HIV can be asymptomatic (without symptoms) for a long time, often 8-10 years without antiretroviral therapy (ART).

list.title: Chronic HIV Infection:
list.snippet: During this stage, HIV continues to multiply in the body, but at a low level, and may not cause noticeable symptoms.

list.title: AIDS:
list.snippet: AIDS is the most advanced stage of HIV infection, where the immune system is severely weakened. Without treatment, it can take 10 years or longer for HIV to progress to AIDS.

list.title: Treatment (ART):
list.snippet: With ART, people with HIV can live long, healthy lives, potentially for decades, and the virus can be suppressed to undetectable levels, meaning it cannot be transmitted.

list.title: Importance of Testing:
list.snippet: Because many people don't experience noticeable symptoms, getting tested is crucial for early detection and treatment.

related_questions.question: What is the president's emergency program for AIDS relief?
related_questions.snippet: Who We Are. The U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) [1 MB] is the largest commitment by any nation to address a single disease in history, enabled by strong bipartisan support across ten U.S. congresses and four presidential administrations, and through the American people's generosity.
related_questions.title: About Us – PEPFAR - United States Department of State

text_blocks.snippet: The President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) is a U.S. government initiative focused on combating HIV/AIDS globally. Launched in 2003, PEPFAR is the largest global health program dedicated to a single disease and has been instrumental in saving millions of lives and changing the trajectory of the HIV epidemic.
snippet_highlighted_words: The President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) is a U.S. government initiative focused on combating HIV/AIDS globally

list.title: Global Focus:
list.snippet: PEPFAR operates in over 50 countries, with a primary focus on resource-limited settings.

list.title: Comprehensive Approach:
list.snippet: PEPFAR supports a wide range of interventions, including prevention, treatment, care, and health systems strengthening.

list.title: Partnerships:
list.snippet: PEPFAR works in close collaboration with governments, local communities, faith-based organizations, and other stakeholders.

list.title: Results:
list.snippet: PEPFAR has achieved significant results, including providing antiretroviral treatment for millions, preventing new infections, and providing care for vulnerable populations.

list.title: Sustainability:
list.snippet: PEPFAR emphasizes building sustainable health systems and strengthening local capacity to ensure long-term impact.

list.title: Funding:
list.snippet: PEPFAR is funded by the U.S. government and is authorized by Congress.

list.title: Recent Developments:
list.snippet: In December 2022, PEPFAR announced a five-year strategy to accelerate progress towards ending the HIV/AIDS pandemic by 2030.

list.title: Potential Funding Cuts:
list.snippet: There have been recent discussions about potential cuts to PEPFAR funding, which could impact its effectiveness.

list.title: Notable Milestones:
list.snippet: PEPFAR has supported antiretroviral treatment for nearly 20.5 million people and enabled 5.5 million babies to be born HIV-free to mothers living with HIV.
